title: NGINX2Root FAQ: Five vulnerabilities in NGINX (CVE-2026-123007) | Tenable®
summary: F5 patched five critical NGINX RCE vulnerabilities (NGINX2Root) in a November 18 out-of-band release. A public PoC exists for CVE-2026-123007.
body_markdown:
**Frequently asked questions about five critical NGINX remote code execution vulnerabilities and five additional flaws fixed in F5’s November 18 out-of-band release.**


## Key takeaways


1. NGINX2Root is associated with five critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, and a separate, unpatched Linux kernel local privilege escalation (LPE) flaw that can be chained with the NGINX bugs to gain root.
2. CVE-2026-123007 is the most urgent of the five. It is an unauthenticated RCE flaw in NGINX’s HTTP/2 implementation and requires only HTTP/2 over TLS to be enabled. A PoC is publicly available on GitHub.
3. F5’s November 18 release fixed the five NGINX2Root vulnerabilities and five additional NGINX flaws.


## Background


Tenable’s Research Special Operations (RSO) team has compiled this blog to answer Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) regarding NGINX2Root, a set of five critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, and five additional NGINX flaws that F5 fixed in an out-of-band security release on November 18, 2026.


## FAQ


**What is NGINX2Root?**


[NGINX2Root](https://xint.io/blog/nginx2root-remote-code-execution) is the name Xint (Theori) gave to five critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, and a separate, unpatched Linux kernel local privilege escalation (LPE) flaw that[Xint](https://xint.io/blog/nginx2root-remote-code-execution) says can be chained with the NGINX bugs to gain root. The NGINX flaws are memory-corruption bugs in HTTP/2, HTTP/3, the resolver, and the mail proxy module. Exploitation depends on the specific feature being active, and achieving code execution generally requires ASLR to be absent or defeated. The name is not used by[F5](https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000164058) or[nginx.org](http://nginx.org/) .


**What are the vulnerabilities associated with NGINX2Root?**


**CVE** **Description** **CVSSv4 (F5)**


[CVE-2026-123007](https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-123007) NGINX ngx_http_v2_module vulnerability 9.2


[CVE-2026-123633](https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-123633) NGINX ngx_http_v2_module vulnerability 9.2


[CVE-2026-123634](https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-123634) NGINX resolver vulnerability 9.2


[CVE-2026-121810](https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-121810) NGINX ngx_http_v3_module vulnerability 9.2


[CVE-2026-113425](https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-113425) NGINX ngx_mail_proxy_module vulnerability 9.2


Xint also identified a separate, unpatched Linux kernel SCTP use-after-free vulnerability (no CVE assigned as of November 18) that can be chained with these flaws to escalate from NGINX worker access to root. This includes escaping Docker containers to compromise the host kernel. Xint is withholding most technical details pending a kernel patch.


**Which one is the most urgent?**


The most urgent is CVE-2026-123007 because it only needs HTTP/2 to be enabled. It has been in the code since HTTP/2 support arrived in 1.9.5 in 2015, and Wiz confirmed code execution against an NGINX instance serving only static content, with no application logic or additional modules involved. Wiz Research, Rapid7, Xint and others reported it independently.


**When were the NGINX vulnerabilities first disclosed?**


On November 18,[F5 released an out-of -band security update](https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000164058) for 10 vulnerabilities in the NGINX Plus, NGINX Open Source.


**What are the other vulnerabilities fixed in F5’s November 18?**


There are five additional NGINX CVEs affecting NGINX Plus, NGINX Open Source.


**CVE** **Description** **CVSSv4**


[CVE-2026-118899](https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-118899) NGINX TLSv1.3 vulnerability 8.7


[CVE-2026-120993](https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-120993) NGINX ngx_stream_ssl_module vulnerability 6.9


[CVE-2026-125283](https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-125283) NGINX map directive and regex matching vulnerability 6.9


[CVE-2026-123640](https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-123640) NGINX ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module vulnerability 6.9


[CVE-2026-120967](https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-120967) NGINX ngx_stream_ssl_module vulnerability 6.3


**Was this exploited as a zero-day?**


There is no evidence of the five NGINX vulnerabilities being exploited as zero-days. Xint says it found the bugs on October 11, 2026, reported them to F5 via HackerOne on October 16, and published them after the coordinated release. No source reviewed reports exploitation in the wild, and the CVEs are not on CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog as of November 18.


**Are** **threat actors exploiting these CVEs?**


There are no reports of threat actors exploiting these CVEs as of November 18.


**Is there a proof-of-concept (PoC) available for these vulnerabilities?**


Yes for CVE-2026-123007. Rapid7 published a[technical analysis](https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ve-cve-2026-123007-critical-nginx-http-2-integer-underflow-leads-to-rce-fixed/) of CVE-2026-123007 on November 18, and its author, Stephen Fewer, released a public PoC on GitHub at[sfewer-r7/CVE-2026-123007](https://github.com/sfewer-r7/CVE-2026-123007) . The repository includes a minimal crash-level trigger script and a full unauthenticated remote code execution exploit, demonstrated against NGINX 1.31.8 in a Docker container with HTTP/2 over TLS. Rapid7 describes the exploit as constrained: it depends on a glibc memory-copy routine specific to x86-64 builds, requires roughly 128 gigabytes of HTTP/2 traffic, and needs to defeat ASLR by recovering heap addresses from server responses. Execution lands in the NGINX worker process. The exploit is also unlikely to succeed against servers behind HTTP/2-terminating proxies or on connections too slow to deliver the required data volume before NGINX's one-hour connection limit is reached.


Xint published demo videos and said it intentionally omitted the final steps needed to reproduce the full exploits. Wiz confirmed working exploits exist but has chosen not to publish them.


**Are patches or mitigations available for the NGINX2Root vulnerabilities?**


Yes. Patching is the fix. Mitigations are a temporary stopgap, and each covers only some of the vulnerabilities. Upgrade to the fixed versions in the table below. These fix all ten CVEs in F5’s November 18 release. Xint notes that you must restart NGINX after upgrading, because a configuration reload does not replace the running executable.


**NGINX Open Source**


**Affected Versions** **Fixed Versions**


Before 1.30.7 (stable) and 1.31.9 (mainline) 1.30.7 (stable), 1.31.9 (mainline)


The earliest affected version varies by CVE, from 0.5.x for the mail proxy to 1.9.5 for CVE-2026-123007. A bug is only exploitable if the relevant feature is in use.


**NGINX Plus**


**Affected Versions** **Fixed Versions**


R33–R36 and 37.x before fixed releases 37.0.8.1, 37.3.0.1


R33–R36 have no patch available; those customers need to move to a 37.x release. CVE-2026-123633 is also fixed in 37.0.7.1 and 37.2.0.1.


For those organizations that are unable to apply the available patches, the following mitigations can be applied until patching is feasible.


**Feature / Component** **Mitigation** **Covers**


HTTP/2 Disable HTTP/2 CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633 only


HTTP/3 (QUIC) Remove the QUIC/HTTP/3 listeners CVE-2026-121810


Mail proxy Bind mail listeners to loopback or restrict access with a firewall CVE-2026-113425


Resolver with a request-derived proxy_pass Point proxy_pass at a fixed upstream group and turn off mirror where it is not needed CVE-2026-123634


Xint notes that disabling HTTP/2 does not protect against CVE-2026-123634, CVE-2026-121810, and CVE-2026-113425, so it is not advised to use it as a blanket workaround. Additionally, turning off *mirror* does not make a server safe from CVE-2026-123634.


For the unpatched Linux kernel LPE, until a kernel fix is available, Xint recommends blocking the SCTP module on hosts that do not use it.
